## DeepSeek-V4-Flash UD-IQ2_M — GGUF bring-up inventory + llama.cpp-bar BLOCKED (2026-08-03, `CLAIM-DSV4-UDIQ2M-BRINGUP`)

Bringing up `unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF UD-IQ2_M` (90.93 GiB, 3 shards) on the GB10.

**Layout verdict — NATIVE `deepseek4`, not a standard llama.cpp conversion.** `general.architecture=deepseek4`; per-block `ffn_gate_tid2eid` hash tables are PRESENT (hash layers 0/1/2, I32 [6, 129280]), plus the full `hc_*` MHC + `output_hc_*`, the DSA compressor (41 layers) and Lightning-Indexer (21 layers), and the `exp_probs_b` noaux_tc bias (40 layers). 1328 tensors — EXACT match to our name-map (`scripts/check-dsv4-gguf-namemap.py`, 1328/1328). `deepseek4.vocab_size` is the ONLY absent KV and the loader already derives it from `token_embd` (129280). So our loader needed NO layout change, and `tid2eid` is a REQUIRED weight (predetermined token→expert ownership; the gate supplies only weights), not a top-k we could recompute from `ffn_gate_inp`.

**Quant inventory (unsloth per-tensor "dynamic" mix):** F32 662, Q8_0 318, Q5_K 127, IQ2_XXS 84, Q6_K 45, BF16 43, IQ3_XXS 41, I32 3, MXFP4 (id 39) 2, IQ2_S (id 22) 2, Q4_K 1. Every type is covered by our keep-quant + dequant EXCEPT IQ2_S (2 slabs: one `ffn_gate_exps` + one `ffn_up_exps` layer) and MXFP4 (2 `ffn_down_exps` layers). With the multi-shard split reader landed (see STATUS `CLAIM-GGUF-SPLIT-SHARDS`), our engine LOADS through 1324/1328 tensors and throws only on the first IQ2_S expert slab (`gguf dequant: unsupported ggml type 22`); RSS stayed safe (no OOM). Coherent-generation is PENDING an IQ2_S+MXFP4 keep-quant kernel (dequant-expanding the 4 big slabs would add ~17 GiB → ~106 GiB, GB10 OOM-reboot risk, so keep-quant is the memory-safe path).

**llama.cpp reference bar — BLOCKED on this box (tok/s OWED).** No llama.cpp build present supports the `deepseek4` arch: `~/llama.cpp-pr22569` = paged-attention (matiaslin fork), `~/llama.cpp-pr24423` + `~/llama.cpp-pr` = deepseek32 + diffusion; all register only deepseek / deepseek2 / deepseek2-ocr / deepseek32. `llama-cli` on the checkpoint errors `unknown model architecture: 'deepseek4'`. Upstream `deepseek4` support is **ggml-org/llama.cpp PR #24162** (plus antirez's experimental `antirez/llama.cpp-deepseek-v4-flash` fork); neither is built here. Establishing the bar requires building #24162 (fetch + CUDA build), then a single-sequence greedy decode.

## DeepSeek-V4-Flash — vLLM on ONE Spark is INFEASIBLE; DwarfStar/GGUF was HW-forced (2026-07-31, `CLAIM-DSV4-VLLM-INFEASIBLE`)

DeepSeek-V4-Flash has been benchmarked against `ds4` = **DwarfStar** (antirez's self-contained GGUF C engine), never vLLM. Unlike Laguna (which fit vLLM at NVFP4, 67 GiB — see below), DeepSeek **cannot run on vLLM on a single GB10 Spark at all**: every vLLM-loadable checkpoint exceeds the 119 GiB unified pool —

| Checkpoint | Size | vLLM-loadable | Fits 1 Spark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` | ~168 GB | yes (`modelopt_fp4`) | **no** |
| `Intel/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-AutoRound` | ~156 GB | yes (`auto-round`) | **no** |
| `anemll/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-TP2-W4A4` | ~179 GB | yes (TP2, 2 GPUs) | **no** (built for 2) |
| GGUF IQ2_XXS (~2-bit) | ~80 GB | **no** (GB10 build has no `gguf` quant method) | yes |

The model is ~300B+ total params, so even 4-bit weights are 156-168 GB. The only quant that fits one Spark is extreme-low-bit GGUF, which vLLM can't load here. So on one Spark the ONLY feasible engines are GGUF (our engine, DwarfStar, llama.cpp) — **DwarfStar was forced by the hardware, not an off-policy shortcut** (contrast Laguna, where vLLM fit and llama.cpp-only was avoidable). The policy-correct vLLM DeepSeek comparison is OWED but requires **2× GB10 Sparks + TP2** (the anemll checkpoint, ~90 GB/GPU) over the landed NCCL intra-node TP seam — a multi-node effort, not a single-box run. DwarfStar stays a labeled secondary best-in-class-GGUF peer meanwhile.

## Laguna-NVFP4 — decode-isolated host-sync attribution: the 1.9× to vLLM 18.8 is orchestration, not kernels (2026-08-01, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-DECODE-SYNC`)

Marlin-default decode is ~10 tok/s (0.10 s/tok) vs vLLM-NVFP4 18.8 (~1.9×). To attribute the residual byte-exactly, ran two nsys profiles (`laguna-gen --gpu`, GB10, same 6 prompt ids) at max-tokens 20 and 60 and differenced the CUDA API counts — load + prefill + the one-time Marlin repack are fixed, so (60t − 20t)/40 = **per-decode-token** API calls:

| API call | 20-tok | 60-tok | **per decode token** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cudaStreamSynchronize` | 9,627 | 26,907 | **~432** |
| `cudaMemcpyAsync` | 77,033 | 84,553 | **~188** |
| `cudaMalloc` | 72,675 | 72,675 | **0** |
| `cudaFree` | 72,192 | 72,192 | **0** |

**The decode is HOST-SYNC-bound: ~432 `cudaStreamSynchronize` + ~188 `cudaMemcpyAsync` per token, and ZERO malloc/free** (the 72k allocs are identical in both runs → entirely the load-time Marlin repack; the `DBuf` pool already recycles). ~432 syncs = ~9 per-GEMM drains × 48 layers + per-layer activation host↔device round-trips. NOT kernels (the Marlin MoE is vLLM's OWN kernel, compute at parity), NOT malloc. Per AGENTS.md §396 the 1.9× is a specific closable diff, not a ceiling. **Byte-exact lever (confirmed + sized): device-resident decode** (keep the activation on-GPU across all 48 layers → kills the 188 memcpy/token) **+ decode CUDA-graph** (collapse the 432 syncs/token → 1, exactly vLLM's mechanism). No correctness relaxation — it changes only where buffers live, gated on the golden ids staying identical. Executable plan: `.agents/specs/laguna-device-resident-decode.md`. Same "Brick D" class as DeepSeek device-resident decode (task #228).

## Laguna decode KV+attention → shared-framework port, bf16-KV slice: WASH + near-tie break (2026-08-02, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-KV-ATTN-BF16`)

Ported Laguna's private off-framework decode KV/attention toward vLLM parity via the **tractable slice**: convert the per-layer **f32** KV (`LagunaKvCache::k_dev/v_dev`, `LagunaGraph::cache_k/cache_v`) to **bf16** (vLLM's own paged-KV dtype), halving the DRAM bytes the memory-bound `DecodeAttnGqa*` decode kernels stream — inside Laguna's own kernels, SACRED 27B/35B path byte-untouched. (Full `AttnBlock` port OWED: the shared FA2 pure-decode `LaunchDecodeFA2Bf16` THROWS on `window_size.has_value()` and has no post-attn gate hook, so routing Laguna needs per-layer sliding-window + a softplus-head-gate epilogue grown additively — large + SACRED-risky.)

Built clean on GB10 sm_121a (incremental, **7 TUs, 0 warnings**). DGX-gated on `~/laguna-xs-nvfp4`, token-ids `2,785,9626,377,15360,395`, `VT_LAGUNA_RESIDENT_DECODE=1 VT_LAGUNA_DECODE_GRAPH=1` (the ~35 tok/s decode-graph path), max-tokens 128, 2 runs each:

| path | first-20 prefix vs vLLM golden | decode/step (best of 2) |
|---|---|---|
| **base f32 KV** | **MATCH** (`22345 83 268 33586 81 855 397 874 367 6376 815 340 9626 377 15360 83 1729 756 1205 565`) | 3.84s / 127 = **33.1 tok/s** |
| **bf16 KV** | **BREAK** — diverges at token 2 (`…83 22345 395 6885…` vs golden `…83 268 33586…`) | 3.93s / 127 = **32.3 tok/s** |

**WASH on speed** (bf16 3.93s vs base 3.84s; spreads base 3.84–4.03 / bf16 3.93–4.07 overlap → indistinguishable) — did NOT move the residual. At the XS gate's short context (~130 tok) the decode-attention KV read is a small share of decode time; `lm_head_gemv` (streams the ~600 MB tower) + Marlin MoE dominate — so this **confirms the ~17%-to-vLLM-42.46 residual is GEMV/MoE, not KV/attention traffic**, at this context. **Near-tie BREAK on correctness**: bf16 output is coherent (re-emits the golden prefix from ~token 14) but flips the step-2 argmax 268→22345 — our device regime is not bit-identical to vLLM, so a near-tie flips even when moving TOWARD vLLM's bf16 dtype (vLLM itself uses bf16 KV yet emits 268). Two strikes → **NOT landed**; default stays f32 KV (base prefix + ~33 tok/s re-verified after DGX restore). Tested diff + analysis: `.agents/specs/laguna-kv-attn-port-2026-08-02.md`.

## Laguna decode attention-glue fusion — BYTE-EXACT, −4.2% GPU-busy, −120 graph nodes/step (2026-08-02, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-GLUE-FUSED`)

The last real Laguna-NVFP4 decode speed lever + a frameworkization win: fold the tiny, under-occupied attention-glue kernels the decode CUDA graph does NOT hide (device-side ramp/drain of the ~1,195 sequential kernel-nodes/token) into fewer, larger nodes — BYTE-EXACT. Gated behind `VT_LAGUNA_GLUE_FUSED` (default ON, `=0` opts out) for a same-binary A/B. Two folds landed on the resident decode-graph (`LagunaGraph::RunChain`) + the eager resident fallback:

- **L1 — softplus out-gate folded into the attention-combine store.** `SoftplusHeadGateKernel` was a separate pass doing `attn[h,d] *= softplus(g[h])` after the combine wrote `o=acc*inv`. Folding computes the same `(acc*inv)*softplus(g[h])` in registers inside `DecodeAttnCombineKernel` (+ the SPLIT≤1 fallbacks `DecodeAttnGqa{,G}Kernel`) — BYTE-EXACT because the store+reload of the f32 `acc*inv` is lossless. −1 kernel/layer.
- **L4 — residual-Add + STANDARD RMSNorm pairs routed through the shared `vt::FusedChain(kFusedAddRmsNormStd)` seam** (the same machinery qwen3/gemma use): `res += x; out = rms_norm(res)*w`. BYTE-EXACT to `vt::Add + rms_norm_seq`: the f32 residual add is commutative (+ `ResRound<f32>` is identity) and the norm uses the SAME 256-thread strided-sum + shared-tree reduction + `1/sqrtf` as `RmsNormSeqKernel`. NODE-COUNT WIN in the DEFAULT Tier-0 composite (no `VT_FUSED_TIER` needed): the composite collapses `kAdd`+`kRmsNorm` to ONE `vt::RmsNorm(residual)` launch (`RmsNormRowKernel` does the add inline). The post-attn norm folds in place; the last MLP residual add folds with the NEXT layer's input norm (last layer's with the final norm), so both loose per-layer Adds disappear into fused nodes. ≈−2 kernels/layer.
- **C (shared-into-MoeCombine) SKIPPED — provably NOT byte-exact in Laguna.** Unlike qwen3_5 (f32 combine out), Laguna's `MoeCombine` writes **bf16** `dout` then casts to f32, so folding the f32 shared `so` before the bf16 store rounds `(routed+shared)` to bf16 vs the current `bf16(routed)+so_f32` — a bit change. Left as its separate f32 add.
- **L2 (fused qk-norm+RoPE preamble) — NOW LANDED (2026-08-03, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-PREAMBLE-FUSED` below).** The shared `AttnQkNormRopeGate` indexes cos/sin by token, but Laguna's graph decode needs position-from-DEVICE (`*pos_buf`, half-split layout) — landed as a new Laguna-local capture-safe kernel `FusedQkNormRopeGKernel` (4→1 nodes/layer, byte-exact, +0.6% wall).

**BYTE-EXACT GATE (RED-first, `~/laguna-xs-nvfp4`, token-ids `2,785,9626,377,15360,395`, `VT_LAGUNA_RESIDENT_DECODE=1 VT_LAGUNA_MARLIN_MOE=1 VT_LAGUNA_DECODE_GRAPH=1`, max-tokens 160, SAME binary):** `=1` (fused) and `=0` (baseline) produce **byte-identical** 159-token id streams (first-20 `22345 83 268 33586 81 855 397 874 367 6376 815 340 9626 377 15360 83 1729 756 1205 565`). PASS.

**SPEED — paging-immune nsys `cuda_gpu_kern_sum`, `--cuda-graph-trace=node`, 2-length diff `(160−20)/140` = steady decode/step (the GB10 "e2e-wall-is-useless / GPU-busy is the anchor" rule):**

| arm | GPU-busy ms/step | graph nodes/step | wall decode/step (drop_caches, best-of-4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=0` baseline | 28.90 | 1,195 | 4.49s/159 = 35.4 tok/s |
| `=1` fused | 27.69 | 1,075 | 4.48s/159 = 35.5 tok/s |
| **Δ** | **−4.2%** | **−120 (−10%)** | **tied (no regression)** |

The **−120 nodes/step** confirms the folds took effect (48× softplus removed + ~2 norm/add folds/layer collapsed); GPU-busy device time drops **4.2%** — beyond the ~1.5-2.5% ramp/drain estimate, because the fused `RmsNorm(residual)` is itself cheaper than the loose `Add + RmsNorm`. At the wall the two arms are tied (`drop_caches`-standardized 4.48 vs 4.49s; the earlier un-standardized 5.95s reading was pure GB10 reload/paging noise) — the recovered device-time sits inside a graph replay still bounded by the fixed per-step host embed-gather + step-boundary sync. BYTE-EXACT + neutral-to-positive → **landed default-ON**. Repro: `~/laguna_glue_run.sh` (byte-exact) + `~/laguna_glue_nsys.sh` (nsys/wall).

## Laguna decode on-device greedy sample — BYTE-EXACT, removes the per-step host argmax, +0.28% wall (2026-08-02, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-ONDEV-SAMPLE`)

The next Laguna-NVFP4 decode lever + a frameworkization win: the resident decode graph used to `Synchronize` after each replay, return the whole `[100352]` logits vector, and let the greedy driver **argmax on the HOST** over the vocab (then gather the next token's embedding on the host) BETWEEN two graph replays — a GPU-IDLE host round-trip the decode-framework-routing audit flagged as Laguna's off-framework "born on the host" seam. vLLM avoids it with **on-device sampling**. This lever moves both onto the device, INSIDE the captured graph: an on-device greedy argmax (`vt::GreedyArgmax`, two-pass reduction, LOWEST-index tie = the exact winner the host `ArgmaxLastRow` produced) writes the token id to a 1-element device buffer, and a capture-safe `embed_gather` kernel gathers the NEXT step's input embedding from that id — so replay N+1 launches with no host work on step N's logits. WHERE argmax runs changes, NOT the math. Gated `VT_LAGUNA_ONDEV_SAMPLE` (default ON, `=0` opts out) for a same-binary A/B.

- **On-device argmax appended to `LagunaGraph::RunChain`** (after the lm_head write): `GreedyArgmax(logits[1,V] → argmax_id[1] i64)`. Its partials scratch is grown ONCE by the graph's gstate-0 eager warm-run, so no `cudaMalloc` runs inside the gstate-1 capture; fixed pointers ⇒ capture-safe.
- **New capture-safe `embed_gather` kernel** (`cuda_laguna.cu`, added to `LagunaDeviceKernels`) prepended to `RunChain`: `hidden[H] = embed_table[*argmax_id]`, reading the token id from a DEVICE buffer (bf16 table widened `bits<<16` EXACTLY as the host embed loop, f32 copied). The stock `vt::Embedding` is NOT capture-safe (per-call event query/sync + D2H bounds ring), so a dedicated pure-launch kernel was written.
- **Driver seam:** `LagunaGraph::Step` seeds `argmax_id` with this step's input token (an 8-byte host write, replacing the H-element host embed loop) and reads it back after the drain; `LagunaKvCache.last_sampled` surfaces the id so `examples/laguna_gen` skips the host vocab argmax. Only the example driver calls `LagunaForwardGgufCached` (grep-verified); the unit tests use the stateless CPU entry, so default-ON is safe.

**BYTE-EXACT GATE (`~/laguna-xs-nvfp4`, token-ids `2,785,9626,377,15360,395`, `VT_LAGUNA_RESIDENT_DECODE=1 VT_LAGUNA_MARLIN_MOE=1 VT_LAGUNA_DECODE_GRAPH=1`, max-tokens 160, SAME binary):** `=1` (on-device) and `=0` (host argmax) produce **byte-identical** 160-token id streams (first-20 `22345 83 268 33586 81 855 397 874 367 6376 815 340 9626 377 15360 83 1729 756 1205 565`). PASS.

**SPEED — the win is HOST-side, so WALL is the anchor here (nsys per-kernel GPU-busy under-weights a between-replay host gap).** The example driver's `decode:` timer originally placed the host argmax OUTSIDE the timed step (between `s1` and the next `s0`), so it could not see the gap; the timer was corrected to attribute next-token selection to the step (it is real per-step wall between two replays), and a `decode_hp` high-precision line added.

| arm | GPU-busy ms/step (nsys 2-length diff 20↔70, graph-node) | decode wall tok/s (drop_caches, 300-tok, median of 8 paired reps) |
|---|---|---|
| `=0` host argmax | 27.44 | 35.89 |
| `=1` on-device | 27.42 | 35.99 |
| **Δ** | **−0.02 (parity, extra embed+argmax kernels are negligible)** | **+0.28% median (all 8 reps ≥ 0: +0.57/+0.40/+0.22/+0.25/+0.30/+0.45/−0.00/−0.04)** |

GPU-busy is at parity (the added on-device embed + 2 argmax passes cost ~nothing), and the paired drop_caches decode wall is **consistently +0.28%** — the removed ~150 us/step host argmax. Smaller than the ~1.9% a raw "527 us GPU-idle gap" back-of-envelope suggested, because most of that between-replay time is fixed overhead present in BOTH arms (the step-boundary sync + the driver's per-step stderr log); the genuinely removable+attributable slice is the host vocab argmax. BYTE-EXACT + consistently faster + framework-aligning → **landed default-ON**. Repro: `~/laguna-n4-build/gate_byteexact.sh` + `measure_wall2.sh` + `measure_nsys.sh`.

**Lever 2 (lm_head DRAM efficiency) — MEASURED, NOT LANDED (at the M=1 practical floor).** The `LmHeadGemvKernel` `[M=1, N=100352, K=2048]` bf16 (reads `100352×2048×2 = 411 MB`) was profiled from the same `s=0 len=70` nsys run: **avg 2.412 ms/call, med 2.410 ms/call ⇒ 170.4 GB/s (avg) / 170.5 GB/s (med)**, 7.2% of decode GPU time (#5 kernel; the top four are the bf16 projection GEMMs + Marlin MoE). That is 62% of the ~273 GB/s GB10 DRAM ceiling, but that ceiling is a STREAMING number an M=1 GEMV cannot reach (each 4 KB weight row is read once, no reuse); the relevant reference is the prior cuBLAS microbench for this exact M=1×large-N shape at ~2.2 ms (~187 GB/s), and our kernel is **~91% of that** — the realistic headroom is ≤~10% of the lm_head kernel = ≤~0.7% of the step. This matches the prior recorded finding "lm_head optimal" (`laguna-gap-is-gpu-compute-not-host`). Chasing it would require a wider/split-K reduction that reorders the float adds (drops byte-exactness to a near-tie needing a distributional re-gate) for ≤0.7% — **NOT chased, per the "at floor → do not chase" rule.**

## Laguna MoE add_rms_norm fold — BYTE-EXACT −39 AddKernel nodes/step, +0.4% (2026-08-02, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-MOE-ADDNORM`)

A same-tool nsys-vs-nsys diff (ours vs vLLM-NVFP4, both `--cuda-graph-trace=node` on the GB10) put the Laguna-NVFP4 decode at ~90% of vLLM's GPU-busy with the residual gap concentrated in two buckets: the **matmul** bucket (ours ~22.2 ms/tok vs vLLM ~18.5, +3.7) and the **norm** bucket (ours ~0.83 ms/tok of RmsNorm+Add kernels vs vLLM's single fused `add_rms_norm` ~0.13). This lever attacks the norm bucket's one avoidable split; the matmul bucket is analyzed as the Lever-B negative below.

**Lever A — fold the MoE routed-add into the trailing `add_rms_norm` (LANDED, byte-exact).** Under the glue-fused decode graph a MoE layer's residual update runs as TWO graph nodes: `vt::Add(hidden, routed)` (`AddKernel`) then `FusedChain(kFusedAddRmsNormStd)(hn, shared, next_norm, hidden)` (a `RmsNormRowKernel` that adds `shared` inline and normalizes). A new `fused_add2_rmsnorm` device kernel (`cuda_laguna.cu`, added to `LagunaDeviceKernels`) collapses them into ONE node/MoE-layer: `hidden = (hidden + routed) + shared; hn = rms_norm(hidden) * next_norm`. Gated `VT_LAGUNA_MOE_ADDNORM_FUSED` (default ON, `=0` A/B).

- **BYTE-EXACT by construction:** IEEE f32 add is commutative so `(hidden+routed)+shared` equals the split path's `shared+(hidden+routed)` bit-for-bit (`vt::Add` is a plain f32 add; `ResRound<f32>` in `RmsNormRowKernel` is identity), and the sum-of-squares uses the identical 256-thread shared-tree reduction + `1/sqrtf(ss/n+eps)` + `v*inv*w` (non-gemma) as `RmsNormRowKernel`/`RmsNormSeqKernel`.
- **BYTE-EXACT GATE** (`~/laguna-xs-nvfp4`, ids `2,785,9626,377,15360,395`, base env `VT_LAGUNA_RESIDENT_DECODE=1 VT_LAGUNA_MARLIN_MOE=1 VT_LAGUNA_DECODE_GRAPH=1`, max-tokens 160, SAME binary): `=1` and `=0` produce **byte-identical** 160-token streams. PASS.
- **KERNEL SWAP (nsys, 70-tok totals):** `AddKernel` 2.63 ms (2691 inst = 39/tok) → **0**; new `AddAdd2RmsNormStdKernel` 20.02 ms (2691 inst); `RmsNormRowKernel` 38.93 ms (5520 inst = 80/tok) → 20.02 ms (2829 inst = 41/tok). Net add+norm bucket 41.56 → 40.04 ms/69-steps.

| arm | GPU-busy µs/tok (nsys 2-length diff 20↔70, graph-node) | decode wall tok/s (nsys, 70-tok) |
|---|---|---|
| `=0` split (Add + FusedChain) | 27339 | 34.00 |
| `=1` fused (`fused_add2_rmsnorm`) | 27293 | 34.14 |
| **Δ** | **−46 µs/tok GPU (−39 AddKernel nodes/step)** | **+0.4%** |

Small but real and byte-exact — a node-count trim on a graph-captured, GPU-bound decode. Landed default-ON per the parity-enablers policy. Repro: `~/box_leverA.sh`.

**Lever B — carry the decode activation through the projections in bf16 (NOT LANDED — premise does not hold).** The task hypothesis was that our projection GEMV dispatches `internal::gemvx<…, __nv_bfloat16(weight), FLOAT(x)>` plus ours-only `CastBf16`/`CastF32` kernels, and that feeding a bf16 activation would (a) delete the casts and (b) drop the gemvx toward vLLM's `gemvx<bf16,bf16>`. Grounding it on the box:

- **The activation is ALREADY bf16 into the GEMV.** `LagunaGraph::GemmBf16` casts `x`(f32)→bf16 (`ab`) and calls `MatmulBT(ot_f32, ab_bf16, w_bf16)`; `MatmulBTKernelCuda` passes `CUDA_R_16BF` for both operands with `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F`. The `gemvx<bf16, float, float>` template reflects cuBLAS's **f32-OUTPUT** algo choice (it widens the bf16 vector to an f32 accumulator), not an f32 activation in memory.
- **DIRECTLY MEASURED THIS SESSION — the all-bf16 gemvx is NOT faster (EMPIRICAL, paging-robust).** A gated diagnostic (`VT_LAGUNA_BF16_ACTX`) made `GemmBf16` emit the MatmulBT output in bf16 (then cast back), which forces cuBLAS to dispatch the exact **`internal::gemvx<…, __nv_bfloat16, __nv_bfloat16, __nv_bfloat16, float>`** variant vLLM uses (confirmed present in the ACTX=1 nsys). Per-instance avg over 6279+4830 decode gemvx instances @70-tok: **gemvx TOTAL 19961 µs/tok (ACTX=1, all-bf16) vs 19965 µs/tok (ACTX=0, bf16-in/f32-out) — identical within noise (−0.02%)** (algo6 avg 141764 vs 141991 ns; algo7 mix ~unchanged). The projection GEMV is **weight-memory-bound roofline** (the largest qkvg weight ~34 MB bf16 ≈ 142 µs ≈ the 273 GB/s ceiling), so the activation/output dtype is irrelevant to its time. This EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMS `laguna-gap-is-gpu-compute-not-host` ("IDENTICAL cuBLAS gemvx = parity by definition") and refutes the Lever-B premise. The diagnostic arm was also ~15-18% slower in wall (34.3→29.1 tok/s @70-tok nsys) because the cast-back adds kernels — reverted, NOT landed.
- **The projection GEMV is the dominant decode cost** — measured **12.87 + 6.88 = 19.75 ms/tok (72% of the 27.3 ms/tok decode)** plus the `lm_head` GEMV 2.4 ms — the SAME cuBLAS `gemvx` vLLM calls on the same weights. Activation dtype cannot beat cuBLAS parity there.
- **The only removable cost is the cast kernels, ≈1% at NEAR-TIE / invasive risk.** `CastBf16` ≈204 µs/tok + `CastF32` ≈40 µs/tok ≈ **0.9% of decode**. Removing them requires carrying the whole activation/residual stream in bf16, but `hn` feeds not just the cuBLAS projections — it ALSO feeds the **Marlin MoE grouped GEMM** and the **`lm_head` GEMV**, both consuming f32; and the `CastF32` source is a transient bf16 `dout` buffer inside `LagunaMoeResidentMarlinInto` that is fragile to expose under graph capture. So there is no clean byte-exact subset; a full bf16 activation carry is a near-tie change (bf16 residual accumulation) for a ~1% ceiling with a coherence-regression risk against the golden. Given the GEMV is already at cuBLAS parity, **the reward does not justify the near-tie risk — not landed.** The honest matmul-gap closer is a faster M=1 GEMV algo (a separate, still-open lever), not the activation dtype.

## Laguna shared-expert kept fp4 (Marlin W4A16) — near-tie, GPU −2.6% / wall +1.4% (2026-08-03, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-SHARED-FP4`)

The XS-NVFP4 checkpoint stores the per-layer SHARED expert fp4 (`mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj`, `num_bits=4`), and vLLM keeps it fp4 through flashinfer-cutlass. Our default NVFP4 loader (`laguna_weights.cpp` `LnLoadSharedExpertBf16`) DEQUANTIZED it to bf16, so the resident/graph decode read 2 bytes/weight — **4× the DRAM traffic** of vLLM on the DRAM-bound M=1 decode GEMV. **Lever — keep the shared expert fp4-resident and route it through the SAME Marlin W4A16 single-expert (num_experts=1) grouped GEMM the routed experts win on** (the `dense_nvfp4` `GateUpFusedMarlinD` + `MatmulNvfp4MarlinD` primitives, the validated 35B W4A16 path), instead of the bf16 GEMV. bf16 activation, fp4 weight, `scale2` — exactly the routed-expert Marlin regime. ADDITIVE: a new `laguna_shared_fp4.cpp` re-reads the on-disk fp4 bytes into the (else-dead) `shared_{gate,up,down}_proj_fp4` fields from the gen driver BEFORE the shards are released (does NOT touch the SACRED `laguna_weights.cpp`). The decode GEMV drops from the wide fused `router|shared_gate|shared_up` (`N=E+2·moe_I`) to a **router-ONLY** GEMV (split `moe.router`), and the shared gate/up/down ride fp4 Marlin. Gated `VT_LAGUNA_SHARED_FP4` (**default ON**, `=0` opts back out to bf16). CAPTURE-SAFE: the per-weight Marlin residents build on the gstate-0 eager warm-run; pooled DBuf transients are warmed like `LagunaMoeResidentMarlinInto`'s.

**NEAR-TIE, not byte-exact** (fp4 shared ≠ bf16 shared), so gated distributionally, not `=0`-identically:

- **COHERENT + near-tie A/B** (`~/laguna-xs-nvfp4`, ids `2,785,9626,377,15360,395`, base env `VT_LAGUNA_RESIDENT_DECODE=1 VT_LAGUNA_MARLIN_MOE=1 VT_LAGUNA_DECODE_GRAPH=1`, max-tokens 160, SAME binary): `=1` (fp4) and `=0` (bf16) are **byte-identical for the first ~85 tokens** then diverge — a textbook near-tie. Both coherent; the **first-20 ids are identical to the documented golden** (`22345 83 268 33586 81 855 397 874 367 6376 815 340 9626 377 15360 83 1729 756 1205 565`).
- **DISTRIBUTIONAL GATE — PASS 40/40.** vLLM greedy on XS is bf16-NON-deterministic (`~/venvs/vllm-oracle` v0.25.0 LLM API, temp=0, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, `gpu_mem_util 0.40`, 8 runs → **8 unique id streams of 8**). Ours(`=1`) first-40 ids each fall inside vLLM's per-position 8-run candidate set — **40/40 in-distribution.**

**SPEED (fp4 faster, both metrics, clean separation):**

| arm | GPU-busy ms/step (nsys 2-length diff 20↔70, graph-node) | decode wall tok/s (drop_caches, 160-tok, median of 3) |
|---|---|---|
| `=0` bf16 shared GEMV | 27.235 | 35.81 (35.52/35.81/35.81) |
| `=1` fp4 shared Marlin | 26.525 | 36.31 (36.27/36.31/36.39) |
| **Δ** | **−0.71 ms/step (−2.6%)** | **+1.4% (fp4 wins all 3 reps)** |

**KERNEL ATTRIBUTION (per-kernel 2-length diff):** the shared-expert bf16 GEMV bucket (`internal::gemvx`) drops **−1.68 ms/step** (shared gate/up rows removed from the wide GEMV + shared_down GEMV gone), the fp4 Marlin bucket (`marlin_moe_wna16`) adds **+0.90 ms/step** (gate_up fused +0.60, down +0.28), plus +0.09 cast/silu — net **−0.71 ms/step**. The shared expert's decode cost is **~1.68 → ~0.90 ms/step (roughly halved)**, exactly the 4×-fewer-weight-bytes DRAM story. vs vLLM's ~43 tok/s: 83.3% → **84.4%**.

**Memory:** freed the decode-only fused `router|shared_gate|shared_up` projection (~204 MB) > the added fp4 shared tower (~62 MB, 4× smaller than one bf16 shared copy); the bf16 shared copies are KEPT for the T>1 prefill forward (`LagunaFfnBlock`, per-token). Net RSS 22.2 → **22.1 GiB** (small win).

**SCOPE NOTE (honest):** the win is modest because XS's shared expert is SMALL (`shared_expert_intermediate_size = moe_intermediate_size = 512`, `H=2048`) — not the large `[2048→8192]` MLP the initial hypothesis assumed. The lever is real, correct, and default-ON per parity (matches vLLM's fp4 shared), but it is not a large closer; the residual gap is the projection GEMV at cuBLAS parity (Lever-B negative above). Repro: `~/sfp4_gate.sh` + `~/sfp4_vllm_gate.py`.

## Laguna decode qk-norm + RoPE preamble fusion — BYTE-EXACT, 4→1 kernels/layer, −0.17 ms/step GPU, +0.6% wall (2026-08-03, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-PREAMBLE-FUSED`)

Closes the `L2` fold `CLAIM-LAGUNA-GLUE-FUSED` deferred: the decode CUDA graph ran the per-layer attention preamble as FOUR under-occupied M=1 kernel-nodes — `rms_norm_seq(q)` + `rms_norm_seq(k)` + `rope_from_cache_g(q)` + `rope_from_cache_g(k)` (2·nlayers RMSNorm + 2·nlayers RoPE launches/token). This lever collapses them into ONE `fused_qk_norm_rope_g` node/layer — a new **Laguna-local capture-safe kernel** `FusedQkNormRopeGKernel` (one block per head, 256 threads). It reads the decode position from the DEVICE `*pos_buf` and the half-split cos/sin layout `RopeFromCacheGKernel` uses (NOT the shared 35B `AttnQkNormRopeGate`'s token-indexed cache — the exact reason L2 was deferred), and handles the per-layer dual-RoPE regime (global `rotary_dim=64` / sliding `128`) with the per-layer `Hq` (48 global / 64 sliding). Gated `VT_LAGUNA_PREAMBLE_FUSED` (**default ON**, `=0` opts out to the four separate kernels).

**BYTE-EXACT BY CONSTRUCTION — not merely numerically-equivalent.** The kernel REPLICATES the composed path's exact data flow, *including the f32 MEMORY round-trip between the norm and the rope*: **Phase A** = the IDENTICAL 256-thread `sh[256]` Σx² tree as `RmsNormSeqKernel` → the same `inv`; **Phase B** = the `RmsNormSeqKernel` store `(x*inv)*w` written back to the buffer for all `Dh` dims; a **`__syncthreads`**; **Phase C** = the `RopeFromCacheGKernel` rope reading the normed values back from the buffer (`x0=row[i]`, `x1=row[i+half]`, `row[i]=x0*c−x1*s`, `row[i+half]=x1*c+x0*s`) over the `rd/2` pairs. The memory boundary is LOAD-BEARING: a first cut recomputed the normed pair in REGISTERS instead — numerically equivalent, but it let the compiler contract the fused rope `ni*c−nih*s` differently from the standalone rope's `x0*c−x1*s`, which flipped a decode near-tie at token 110 (deterministic). Round-tripping through the buffer + the barrier forces bit-identical arithmetic.

**BYTE-EXACT GATE (`~/laguna-xs-nvfp4`, token-ids `2,785,9626,377,15360,395`, base env `VT_LAGUNA_RESIDENT_DECODE=1 VT_LAGUNA_MARLIN_MOE=1 VT_LAGUNA_DECODE_GRAPH=1`, max-tokens 160, SAME binary):** `=1` (fused) and `=0` (baseline) produce **byte-identical 160-token id streams** (first-20 `22345 83 268 33586 81 855 397 874 367 6376 815 340 9626 377 15360 83 1729 756 1205 565`). Determinism verified so the match is a true bit-equality (not a coincidental near-tie): `=0`×3 and `=1`×3 are each run-to-run identical. PASS.

**SPEED (nsys `cuda_gpu_kern_sum --cuda-graph-trace=node`, 2-length diff 20↔70, paging-immune):** the preamble norm+rope kernels collapse from **160 launches/tok @ 326 µs/tok** (`RmsNormSeqKernel` 80 + `RopeFromCacheGKernel` 80) to **40 launches/tok @ 154 µs/tok** (`FusedQkNormRopeGKernel`) — **−171 µs/tok (−0.17 ms/step) on this bucket, 4→1 nodes/layer**. All decode-scaling kernels: **26.53 → 26.37 ms/step (−0.166 ms/step)**, with no other kernel perturbed (the dominant projection GEMVs at 11.4 + 6.7 ms/tok are untouched — the saving is exactly the preamble bucket). Wall drop_caches (160-tok, median of 3): **36.42 → 36.64 tok/s (+0.6%, fused wins all 3 paired reps)**. vs vLLM ~43 tok/s: 84.7% → **85.2%**.

**SCOPE NOTE (honest):** modest by design — the preamble is ~1.2% of the 26.5 ms/step decode; the dominant cost stays the bf16 projection GEMVs at cuBLAS parity (Lever-B negative above). The win is the graph-node / launch-count reduction (the same ramp/drain residual mechanism the glue fusion exploits), byte-exact, default-ON per parity. Repro: `~/preamble_gate.sh` (byte-exact + wall) + `~/speed2.sh` (nsys 2-length).

## DeepSeek-V4-Flash — decode nsys attribution: 13.0 tok/s, Q8_0 GEMV is 53.5% (2026-08-01, `CLAIM-DSV4-DECODE-NSYS`)

Re-measured the GGUF decode from scratch (`deepseek-v4-gen --gpu --kv-cache`, `ds4flash.gguf` = `IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8`, GB10, tmux drop-proof capture). **Decode = 13.0 tok/s** (0.076 s/step, dead-consistent over 23 steps) vs **ds4 16.5 → 79% of ds4, ~1.27× behind.** The prior-recorded **8.0 baseline is STALE** (device-resident decode + tuned glue landed since; superseded). Prefill 0.47s, PEAK RESIDENT 86.3 GiB.

The MHC glue (`MhcPreFinish`/`MhcPreDots`/`MhcPost`) is 11% of decode GPU time (`CLAIM-DSV4-DECODE-NSYS`, 221 ms/step) and ran its mix dot-products + sqrsum/norm reductions in **FP64**, which GB10 throttles to ~1/32–1/64 of FP32. Gated `VT_V4_MHC_FUSED` (**default ON** per parity-enablers-ship-as-defaults; `=0` restores the bit-faithful FP64 double path for a same-binary A/B). Read once process-wide so the captured decode graph bakes a consistent path.

- **Bit-exact on GB10:** decode ids token-IDENTICAL `VT_V4_MHC_FUSED=1` vs `=0` on the real IQ2XXS UD checkpoint. The unit gate is a CHARACTERIZED near-tie (float reduction reorder vs the round-trip reference, `RelL2 < 1e-3`, `test_cuda_deepseek_v4` "MHC + router in place == round-trip (Brick B)"); both the float and double paths hold well within tolerance at the tiny unit shape.

## DeepSeek-V4-Flash — norm+RoPE FP64→FP32 fold: 14.02→14.87 tok/s (+6.1%), byte-exact (2026-08-03, `CLAIM-DSV4-ROPE-FLOAT`)

The fused per-head-q / kv / inverse-o norm+RoPE kernel (`NormRopeRowsKernel`, Brick-7, the resident-decode default) was already a single launch but ran in **FP64**: the RMS block-reduce in double, the RoPE `pow`/`cos`/`sin` in double, AND each pair's theta recomputed by a DOUBLE `O(pairs²)` left-fold recurrence (`for j<p: theta_extrap *= theta_scale`). GB10 throttles FP64 transcendentals to ~1/32–1/64 of FP32. New `NormRopeRowsFloatKernel` is a 1:1 float mirror of the double kernel AND of ds4's `head_rms_norm_rope_tail_kernel` (`~/w8run/ds4/ds4_cuda.cu:5873`) + `dsv4_qkv_rms_norm_rows_kv_rope_kernel` (`:5779`): float RMS reduce (`rsqrtf`), `powf`/`cosf`/`sinf`, and ds4's **DIRECT** `powf(base, -i/r)` per pair (`i=2p` ⇒ `powf(base,-2p/r) == theta_scale^p`, so the algebra is identical — only the accumulation precision + the per-pair cost change). NO ds4 `attn_factor`/`mscale` (we have none, matching the double kernel). Gated `VT_V4_ROPE_FLOAT` (**default ON** per parity-enablers-ship-as-defaults; `=0` restores the bit-faithful FP64 path for a same-binary A/B). Read once process-wide so the captured decode graph bakes a consistent path. Same launch signature (`grid=(rows)`, block=256) ⇒ no call-site change.

- **Byte-exact:** decode ids token-IDENTICAL `VT_V4_ROPE_FLOAT=1` vs `=0` on the real IQ2XXS UD checkpoint (60 tok, both coherent "…Paris."). Unit gate: characterized near-tie vs the double split `{rms_norm_rows ; rope}` path (`RelL2 < 1e-3`, `test_cuda_deepseek_v4` Brick 7; full suite 20/20·67073 on GB10).
- **Fused kernel time: 4.576 → 0.459 ms/step** (nsys 2-length 40↔140 diff, `--trace=cuda --cuda-graph-trace=node`; whole-run `NormRopeRowsKernel` 178.6M→636.2M ns / `…FloatKernel` 18.2M→64.0M ns; per-step = Δtotal/100). **~10×**, 6.4% → 0.7% of GPU time. 129 launches/step (3 sites × 43 layers) unchanged.
- **Decode 14.02 → 14.87 tok/s (+6.1%, 3 tight reps each — float 14.87/14.89/14.86, double 14.01/14.03/14.02 — 200-tok single-load, VT_V4_RESIDENT_DECODE+DECODE_GRAPH) → 85.0% → 90.1% of ds4 ~16.5** (exceeds the ~14.7 lever-3 target). NOTE: e2e wall-clock on GB10 needs the steady 200-tok reps — a single 60-tok run read 14.26 vs 14.37 (graph-capture/noise-masked); the nsys kernel diff is the authoritative before/after. BAR CORRECTED (2026-08-04): the ratio is now against the same-session ds4-bench.csv `gen_steady_tps 16.5` (flat across configs). The earlier "fixed 17.13 anchor" was WRONG — 17.13 was an UNREPRODUCED variance-peak (box max 16.72, no measurement log); the same-session one-shot `generation 15.39 t/s` is ds4's WORST session (ds4 swings ~9% run-to-run), not its bar. See the MHC-SINK4 BAR CORRECTION note.

## DeepSeek-V4-Flash — MHC-pre finish occupancy + sqrsum-fold: +0.7% byte-exact; ds4-parity MHC launch-bounded (2026-08-03, `CLAIM-DSV4-MHC-LEAN`)

Lever 2. With norm+RoPE folded (lever 3 above), the post-fold nsys attribution makes `MhcPreFinishFloatKernel` the #1 non-GEMM decode kernel: **9.5% of GPU time, ~6.4 ms/step**, launched `<<<1,256>>>` — ONE block (one SM) run **86× SEQUENTIALLY per step** (2 MHC sub-blocks × 43 layers, data-dependent across layers → cannot overlap). It streamed the residual (flat=hc·H) TWICE — once for the sqrsum reduction, once (strided) for the pre-weighted sum. Two ds4-aligned micro-levers, gated `VT_V4_MHC_LEAN` (default ON=1024; `=0`→256 baseline; explicit `512` selectable), read once process-wide:

1. **Occupancy:** widen the lone finish block 256→1024 threads (8→32 warps) to keep more loads in flight on its single SM.
2. **sqrsum fold:** `MhcPreDotsFloatKernel` block 0 also reduces Σresidual² (it already streams the whole residual for its dot) into `mixes[hc3]`; the finish reads that instead of re-streaming the residual — the ds4 mix-stage rms fold. The relocated reduction is the SAME 256-thread block-tree over the same residual ⇒ byte-exact.

- **Byte-exact:** decode ids token-IDENTICAL `VT_V4_MHC_LEAN=1024` vs `=0` (60 tok, coherent). Unit gate `test_cuda_deepseek_v4` 20/20·67073 (the wide-block norm reorder is a characterized `RelL2<1e-3` near-tie).
- **`MhcPreFinish` 6.52 → 5.98 ms/step (−8.3%)** (nsys 2-length 40↔140 diff; block-bump-alone was −5.8% at 6.43→6.06, the fold added ~−2.5%).
- **Decode 14.85 → 14.96 tok/s (+0.7%, 3 tight reps each: base 14.85/14.86/14.84, lean 14.95/14.96/14.98) → 90.0% → 90.7% of ds4 ~16.5** (bar corrected from the unreproduced 17.13 anchor; measured tok/s unchanged).

**HONEST BOUND (the important finding):** the finish kernel barely moved despite 4× the warps AND a removed memory pass — so it is **not warp-latency- or memory-pass-bound; it is floored by the 86 sequential single-block launches** (each ~70 µs of irreducible per-call latency: scheduling + the thread-0-serial Sinkhorn barrier + the mandatory `__syncthreads` chain that serializes the single block). The aspirational "fuse the whole MhcPre stack (dots+finish+post) into ONE kernel mirroring ds4's `hc_split_weighted_sum_norm_fused_kernel`" would cut 258→86 MHC launches/step but must then run the 24 mix-dots SERIALLY inside one block (likely net-negative on the dots) and still leaves the ~6 ms finish core single-block — and it is numerics-delicate (distributional gate). ds4's own `hc_split_weighted_sum_norm_fused_kernel` is ALSO `<<<n_rows,256>>>` = one block per row at decode, yet cheaper per call; closing that gap needs an ncu per-call breakdown of ds4's kernel + a layer-chain-spanning MHC restructure (high-risk), the owed residual. Lever 2 ships the measured byte-exact +0.7%; the Q8_0 GEMV (#1, 37.8%) remains untouched and at-parity.

**Integration re-verify (2026-08-03, GB10 sm_121a, clean CUDA+Triton Release build off `6576814b`).** Both decode glue-fold levers cherry-picked clean and re-gated on a fresh GB10 build: build **EXIT 0**; **SACRED `test_qwen36_paged_engine` 315/315 (0 failed, UNMOVED — the DeepSeek-only change does not touch the 35B path)**; `test_cuda_deepseek_v4` **20/20·67073**. **Byte-exact re-confirmed on the resident-decode path** (`deepseek-v4-gen --gpu --kv-cache` on `~/w8run/ds4/ds4flash.gguf` IQ2XXS): decode ids token-IDENTICAL for `VT_V4_ROPE_FLOAT=1`/`=0` AND `VT_V4_MHC_LEAN=1024`/`=0`. ## DeepSeek-V4-Flash — MHC-pre finish hc=4 register-resident Sinkhorn + norm-fold: +4.6% byte-exact, 91.3%→95.5% of ds4 ~16.5 (2026-08-03, `CLAIM-DSV4-MHC-SINK4`, GB10 sm_121a)

Closes the owed residual `CLAIM-DSV4-MHC-LEAN` flagged (its "closing that gap needs an ncu per-call breakdown of ds4's kernel"). **STEP 1 — ncu the mechanism (locked-clock GB10, M=1, standalone microbench of the exact default kernels):** the finish is **neither compute (SM 0.08–0.17%) nor bandwidth (Mem Busy 0.27–0.50%) bound** — it is **single-block serial-latency bound**. `Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction` = 149 (baseline), of which **~86% is stall "waiting for sibling warps at a CTA barrier"** (`__syncthreads`) and **~42% scoreboard-stall on an L1TEX operation**. Root cause: ptxas hands the generic runtime-`hc` finish a **2048-byte LOCAL stack frame** (the `cl[256]/m[256]` Sinkhorn arrays — dynamic index ⇒ off-chip local memory; ncu "only 4.0 of 32 bytes" per local transaction), so thread 0 grinds the 20-iter Sinkhorn through scattered local-DRAM while the other 31 warps idle at the barrier. **This overturns the prior "~70 µs of irreducible per-call latency" bound: the thread-0-serial-Sinkhorn barrier was REAL but the local-memory Sinkhorn under it was REDUCIBLE.** Widening 256→1024 (the −8% lean fix) never touched it — more warps just idle harder at the same barrier.

**ds4's cheaper mechanism (file:line):** `hc4_split_one` (`~/w8run/ds4/ds4_cuda.cu:9618`) runs the split with a **fully-unrolled `float c[16]` (n_hc==4 hardcoded)** — register-resident, no local memory; `hc_split_weighted_sum_norm_fused_kernel` (`:9752`) folds the RMSNorm Σ into the weighted-sum loop single-pass (`sum += acc*acc`, no layer_out re-read).

**STEP 2 — port (byte-exact for the structural hc=4):** `MhcPreFinishFloatKernel4` + `SinkhornInplace4` (hardcoded 4×4 + `#pragma unroll` ⇒ **ptxas 2048→0-byte stack frame**, all registers) with the ds4 norm-fold. Identical op sequence/accumulation order to `SinkhornInplace` for hc=4, so BYTE-IDENTICAL (not a near-tie). Gated `VT_V4_MHC_SINK4` (**default ON** per parity-enablers; `=0` = generic finish, same-binary A/B); engages only when `hc==4` (any other hc keeps the generic path). Same 1024-wide finish block + sqrsum fold as the LEAN default, so the norm reduction tree is unchanged.

- **Byte-exact:** standalone A/B (400 launches, fixed seed) `comb` + `layer_out` **0/16 ULP** mismatch. E2E resident-decode path (`deepseek-v4-gen --gpu --kv-cache`, IQ2XXS 85 GiB): decode ids **token-IDENTICAL** `VT_V4_MHC_SINK4=1` vs `=0` (24 tok: `11111 16 455 6102 294 8760 344…` → "Paris. The capital of France is Paris…").
- **Kernel µs/call (ncu, locked clocks 3003 MHz):** **~75 → ~26 µs/call** (median, `gpu__time_duration`); event-loop (sustained clock, incl. launch overhead) **95.1 → 56.6 µs/call**. ptxas stack frame **2048 → 0 bytes**.
- **Decode (paired, worker parked + `drop_caches` + `flock`, 3 arms one session):** VT_V4_PROF steady per-step **62 → 59 ms/step (−4.8%)** (rock-steady steps 12–22, both OPT reps identical); whole-decode **15.07 → 15.76 tok/s (+4.6%)**, two OPT reps 15.758/15.747 (Δ0.07% ≪ the +4.6% effect). **→ 91.3% → 95.5% of ds4 ~16.5** (session-stable ~15.87 tok/s = ~96%; bar corrected from the unreproduced 17.13 anchor — see note below).

**VERDICT — the per-call gap is MEASURABLY narrowed but not fully closed.** The reducible part (local-memory Sinkhorn) is gone byte-exact; DeepSeek is now **~96% of ds4** (session-stable ~15.87 tok/s against the corrected ~16.5 bar; honestly ~4% BEHIND, not at/above — the residual is the Q8_0 projection-GEMV weight-stream floor). The residual (opt ~26 µs/call vs ds4 ~7 µs) is the **fundamental single-block `__syncthreads` floor**: thread-0 gates+Sinkhorn → barrier → weighted-sum is a genuine intra-call data dependency ds4 shares but runs leaner (256 threads, tighter global buffers). Fully closing to ds4's 7 µs needs the high-risk **layer-chain-spanning MHC restructure** (batch the 86 sequential MHC calls across layers) that the RAW cross-layer residual dependency blocks — NOT pursued (out of scope, numerics-delicate, distributional-gate). The Q8_0 GEMV (#1, ~37–53%) remains at-parity.

**BAR CORRECTION (2026-08-04) — the ds4 denominator is ~16.5 tok/s, NOT 17.13.** Every `% of ds4` figure in this DeepSeek-V4 decode section is now against **~16.5 tok/s**, the fair same-session ds4 bar (`ds4-bench.csv gen_steady_tps 16.5`, flat across ctx 512-2048 / n 60-200 / the GB10-no-op reserve config). The prior **17.13 anchor was an UNREPRODUCED variance-peak**: the box max is 16.72, it carries no measurement log, and it entered only as a bare denominator in commit `d5dbd581` with no fresh ds4 run (it is ds4's variance-peak / GPU-active-17.6 figure, not a steady bar). ds4's own greedy swings ~9% run-to-run (15.39 low outlier ↔ 16.72); the same-session `generation 15.39 t/s` is ds4's WORST session, NOT our bar. Against ~16.5, our session-stable **~15.87 tok/s = ~96% of ds4** — honestly **~4% BEHIND** (not at/above), the residual being the Q8_0 projection-GEMV weight-stream floor (7 proven-flat levers). The per-lever ratios above were recomputed onto ~16.5 (measured tok/s unchanged; e.g. SINK4 15.76/16.5 = 95.5%, session-stable 15.87/16.5 = 96.2%). ## Laguna-S-2.1 (`LagunaForCausalLM`) FIRST real vLLM bar — vLLM NVFP4 vs our GGUF (2026-07-31, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-VLLM-NVFP4`)

Until now every Laguna number was measured against **llama.cpp** (the same UD-Q4_K_XL GGUF), and even the correctness oracle was `llama-cli` (`run_oracle.sh`) — vLLM, the project's standing bar, had **never** been run on Laguna. This closes that gap.

**vLLM Laguna-S-2.1 (single GB10, greedy, `enforce_eager`, prompt "The capital of France is"):**
- Checkpoint: official `poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4` (`compressed-tensors` NVFP4, ~67 GiB, fits the 119 GiB unified pool).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| llama.cpp | GGUF Q4_K_XL | — | 27.8 |

vLLM is ~2.4× our GGUF path. llama.cpp still leads both at batch-1 (its GGUF GEMV is best-in-class for single-request latency; vLLM's edge is throughput under concurrency, not exercised here). ## Laguna-S-2.1 (`LagunaForCausalLM`) W7 decode-speed ATTRIBUTION (profile-only): where the 18x to llama.cpp goes (2026-07-31, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-W7-SPEED`)

Research-only `nsys` profile of the W6 decode (`laguna-gen --gpu`, real 3-shard UD-Q4_K_XL, GB10,
1 prefill + 7 steady decode). Our decode is 0.66 s/tok cold (1.5 tok/s), 0.53 s/tok warm here; the
llama.cpp Poolside-fork runs the IDENTICAL GGUF at 27.8 tok/s (a ~15-18x gap). Token stream matched
the W6 golden. NO code changed; the levers are the follow-on.

MEASURED split (nsys, 5.14 s forward wall):

- **GPU active only 32.7%** of the step (kernel total 1.682 s); host / idle **67.3%**.
- `cudaStreamSynchronize`: 1.729 s over **22,115 calls** (~2,764 per step) = the host FULLY blocked,
  ZERO GPU overlap. `cudaLaunchKernel` only 2.1% (launch overhead is NOT the bottleneck). No H2D/D2H
  copies (unified memory; the GPU reads host vectors in place, so it is NOT copy-bound).
- Root cause: `LagunaForwardGgufCached` issues ~1,795 keep-quant GEMMs/token, each followed by a
  `DrainQueue` sync (`LqGemm`/`LqGemmRowSlice`, no `defer_sync`), with all glue (RMSNorm, dual-RoPE,
  attention, softplus gate, router, SwiGLU) scalar on the HOST between them. The 30 routed experts/
  layer run as UN-GROUPED per-expert GEMVs.
- Of the 32.7% GPU time, **39.4% is `QuantizeQ8K` (activation quant), not the weight matmul** (the
  hidden row is re-quantized once per GEMM); the weight GEMMs themselves run at ~22% of the 240 GB/s
  peak. llama.cpp reads the same ~6.58 GB/token at ~76% of peak.

Ranked levers (all in-tree from the DeepSeek-V4 device-decode campaign): 1. device-resident decode
(kill the ~2,764 syncs, glue on-device) 1.5 -> ~5-7 tok/s; 2. grouped expert GEMM
(`MatmulBTQuantGrouped` + fused gate/up/SwiGLU) +1.5-2x and dedupes the activation-quant; 3. capture
the decode CUDA graph; 4. tuned MMVQ BW; plus free host cleanups (`LagunaEmbed` copies the whole
1.23 GB embed table per token to gather one row; the RoPE cos/sin caches are rebuilt every token).
Honest reachable ~13-20 tok/s (8-13x), 27.8 a stretch (same shape as ds4's host -> ~12.7 outcome).
See `.agents/specs/laguna-s21-w7-speed-2026-07-31.md`.

## Laguna-S-2.1 (`LagunaForCausalLM`) W6 — KV cache + incremental decode: 5.05× faster, token-identical (2026-07-31, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-W6`)

W6 kills W5's O(n²) stateless full-recompute. A per-layer K/V cache
(`LagunaKvCache`) + a single-token incremental-decode forward
(`LagunaForwardGgufCached`) attends each new token over cached K/V instead of
re-running the whole context every step. Same binary A/B on the real 3-shard
`UD-Q4_K_XL` GGUF (GB10, `--gpu`, keep-quant), greedy, prompt "The capital of
France is", 24 tokens (drop_caches, `flock`, one model resident, worker down):

```
$ laguna-gen --model Laguna-S-2.1-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00003.gguf --gpu --stateless --max-tokens 24   # W5
    ids  22345 83 350 785 989 395 13259 330 4159 9431 377 340 4328 377 444 136 22029 9626 71 493 6396 565 7760 10291
    prefill 1.37s | decode 76.60s | TPOT 3.33 s/tok over 23 steps   (per-step GREW 0.68s→5.08s: the O(n²) signature)

$ laguna-gen --model Laguna-S-2.1-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00003.gguf --gpu --max-tokens 24                # W6 (default, KV-cache)
    ids  22345 83 350 785 989 395 13259 330 4159 9431 377 340 4328 377 444 136 22029 9626 71 493 6396 565 7760 10291
    prefill 1.47s | decode 15.10s | TPOT 0.66 s/tok over 23 steps   (FLAT ~0.66–0.69 s/tok, context-independent)
```

- **TOKEN-IDENTICAL GATE: PASS.** The two `generated ids` lines are BYTE-EQUAL
  (identical md5 `754728c6…`) and both equal the recorded W5 golden — a KV cache
  changes nothing numerically when correct. Bit-exact on the first run; no cache
  bug. The recompute path itself is unchanged (shared `LagunaAttention`/
  `LagunaFfnBlock` helpers; its ids still match the W5 golden after the refactor).
- **SPEED: decode 3.33 → 0.66 s/tok = 5.05×.** Prefill unchanged (~1.4s), peak
  resident 71.09 GiB (119 GiB pool).
- **Mechanism:** post-QK-RMSNorm/post-RoPE K + raw V cached at f32 (RoPE/QK-norm
  are position-only, attention is causal → the cached K/V equal what the recompute
  recomputes). MIXED attention per-layer: 12 GLOBAL layers keep full history; 36
  SLIDING-WINDOW-512 layers EVICT rows beyond the 512 window (gemma2/3
  `is_sliding`) — the memory cap; the `pi-pj≥window` mask keeps correctness
  independent of eviction (window not exceeded at 30 ctx tokens, so eviction is a
  no-op here — the >512-ctx exercise is future).
- **Next speed (owed, not this row):** grouped-expert GEMM + device-resident
  decode chain (both in-tree from ds4); token-exact-vs-llama.cpp tightening.
- See `.agents/specs/laguna-s21-w6-2026-07-31.md`.

## Laguna-S-2.1 (`LagunaForCausalLM`) W5 RUNNABLE — real keep-quant GGUF forward, coherent on GB10 (2026-07-31, `CLAIM-LAGUNA-W5`)

W5 makes Laguna **RUNNABLE**: `examples/laguna-gen` loads the REAL 3-shard unsloth
`UD-Q4_K_XL` GGUF (keep-quant) and greedy-generates COHERENT text on the GB10.

```
$ laguna-gen --model Laguna-S-2.1-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00003.gguf \
             --prompt "The capital of France is" --max-tokens 24 --gpu
[gen] LOADED: layers=48 experts=256 vocab=100352 has_gguf=1 | load 20.6s | RSS 69.8 GiB PEAK 69.8 GiB
prompt: The capital of France is
generated ids: 22345 83 350 785 989 395 13259 330 4159 9431 377 340 4328 377 444 136 22029 9626 71 493 6396 565 7760 10291
generated text:  Paris.\n\nThe user is seeking a detailed explanation of the concept of "cultural capital" as developed by French soci
prefill: 1.36s  decode: 75.14s  TPOT 3.27s/tok over 23 steps  PEAK RESIDENT: 71.08 GiB
```

- **COHERENCE GATE PASSES.** The first generated token is **" Paris."** — matching
  the llama.cpp-Poolside reference on the identical UD-Q4_K bytes ("…Paris.") — and
  the continuation is fully coherent English. Coherence = the RUNNABLE bar (gate a).
- **Memory:** peak 71 GiB in the 119 GiB GB10 unified pool (113 GiB free before the
  run); the 256 routed experts + attention/dense/shared/lm_head GEMM weights stay
  block-COMPRESSED (Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K/Q8_0), consumed keep-quant via `vt::MatmulBT`
  (CUDA `kMatmulBTQuant`); only norms/router/bias/embed dequant to f32.
- **What landed:** a loader-local **multi-shard GGUF reader** (`LagunaGgufCtx` routes
  each of the 814 tensors to its shard — shard-1 is header/KV only), **params-from-KV**
  (`LagunaParamsFromGguf`: per-layer head_count array, dual-rope keys, MoE keys),
  the **keep-quant tower** (`LoadLagunaFromGgufShards`, ds4 `Mw`/`Sew`/`Vec` precedent),
  **`LagunaForwardGguf`** (the f32 composition with the ~9 GEMM sites swapped to
  keep-quant `LqGemm`/`LqGemmRowSlice`, ds4 `Gemm`/`GemmRowSlice` precedent), and the
  **`examples/laguna_gen`** run entrypoint (mirrors `deepseek_v4_gen`).
- **Speed (W6, owed):** 3.27 s/tok is a STATELESS full-recompute reference (per-token,
  per-expert GEMV, no KV cache) — a KV-cached forward + grouped-expert GEMM
  (`MatmulBTQuantGrouped`, the ds4 path) is the throughput lane, not a correctness gap.
- See `.agents/specs/laguna-s21-w5-2026-07-31.md`.

W4 FETCHED the unsloth `UD-Q4_K_XL` GGUF (73.4 GiB, 3 shards) to the DGX and read
its metadata + full tensor map AUTHORITATIVELY (814 tensors, split.count=3, arch
`laguna`). This surfaced three fidelity corrections to the W1-W3 scaffold, each
grounded in the real GGUF + llama.cpp (NOT config.json): per-head QK-RMSNorm

## OLMo-2 full-width qk-norm+rope fold — Tier-D3 (2026-07-31, `CLAIM-D3-OLMO2-FULLWIDTH-QKNORM`) - CONSISTENCY/SHARED-CATALOG fold, bit-exact (CPU RED-first gated; DGX SACRED OWED)

Tier-D3 of the cross-arch merged-GEMM/glue fold plan (`.agents/specs/arch-fusion-fold-plan-2026-07-30.md`). OLMo-2's FULL-WIDTH q/k RMSNorm (`_apply_qk_norm`, olmo2.py:113-117,160-172 — RMSNorm over the WHOLE q-dim/k-dim, all heads folded into ONE variance statistic, distinct from the per-head head_dim norm) + standard NeoX RoPE preamble folds onto the SHARED FusedChain glue catalog. **The shape-param generalization:** `FStep` gains a `norm_full_width` structural flag (`include/vt/fused_recipe.h`, additive, default false = per-head Dh → EVERY existing recipe byte-identical), and a new sibling recipe `kAttnQkNormRopeFullWidth` (`include/vt/recipes.h`) sets it on its two RMSNorm steps — the full-width variant of Qwen3-dense's `kAttnQkNormRope`, SAME operand table / step wiring, only the bound norm SHAPE differs (operand 0/2 = `[T,qdim]`/`[T,kdim]` with a full-width `[qdim]`/`[kdim]` weight, vs the per-head `[.,Dh]`/`[Dh]`). `olmo2.cpp` `Olmo2AttnBlock` routes through `vt::FusedChain(kAttnQkNormRopeFullWidth, ...)` when RoPE runs from a cache (YaRN full-attn layers / the default-ON bf16 cos-sin cache); the in-place `RopeNeox` fallback (`VT_QWEN3_ROPE_CACHE=0`) keeps the standalone sequence (mirrors the qwen3.cpp guard — the recipe's third step is RopeFromCache, so routing RopeNeox through it would swap RoPE impls). Realization: **composite-only** (`fast_op=kNoFastOp`) — the per-head `kAttnQkNormRope` bespoke fast kernel (Metal-registered) assumes a Dh reduction, so the full-width variant does not claim it; a full-width fast kernel is a clean follow-up perf step. **Additive/inert:** `kAttnQkNormRope` (per-head, fast_op intact) is UNTOUCHED → qwen3/27B byte-identical; the `norm_full_width` field defaults false so every prior recipe is unchanged.

**Bit-exact by construction, PROVEN on CPU.** Because the Tier-0 composite's `RmsNorm` reduces over the bound row's last dim (device-agnostic — the SAME walker on CPU and CUDA), the composite realizes the full-width norm BYTE-EXACTLY with NO new primitive: it dispatches the EXACT standalone `RmsNorm(q,[qdim]) + RmsNorm(k,[kdim]) + RopeFromCache` sequence OLMo-2 hand-called before the fold. `tests/vt/test_ops_fused_chain.cpp` new case `kAttnQkNormRopeFullWidth composite == full-width RmsNorm(q)+RmsNorm(k)+RopeFromCache` byte-compares (raw f32 memcmp) the composite against the standalone full-width sequence across MHA + GQA + head_dim 64/128 shapes, RED-first (the full-width result is proven DISTINCT from a per-head Dh norm, so a wrong-domain realization fails the byte-check). The FULL `test_ops_fused_chain` suite is **10/10 · 379 assertions** GREEN under the new `FStep` ABI (the per-head `kAttnQkNormRope` regression + all 10 catalog recipes intact ⇒ the shape-param is additive). `olmo2.cpp` + the CPU vt runtime rebuild `-Werror` clean.

Gate status:
- **CPU (this box, mudler-ubuntu-box, `VLLM_CPP_CUDA=OFF`):** `test_ops_fused_chain` **10/10 · 379** (D3 full-width case + per-head regression + all recipes), RED-first bit-exact. Build `-Werror` clean (olmo2.cpp fold + 26 vt CPU TUs rebuilt with the grown `FStep`).
- **DGX (GB10 sm_121a, RelWithDebInfo + cutlass-4.5.0 + triton) — OWED, NOT RUN this pass:** `test_olmo2_paged_engine` SACRED (`olmo2_greedy_1b`, 16/16) + shared-catalog canaries `test_qwen3_paged_engine` 0.6B/4B + `test_qwen27_paged_engine` 235/235. This lane executed on a CPU-only dev box (no GPU, no cutlass, DGX unreachable), so the empirical GPU SACRED run could not be performed. The fold is bit-exact BY CONSTRUCTION on CUDA (composite-only realization = the identical device-agnostic walker the CPU byte-check pins; OLMo-2's committed default rope path is cache-based ⇒ the fold fires and the composite == the pre-fold standalone sequence), but per project discipline a pass ≠ the code ran — the DGX SACRED gate is owed before D3 is fully closed.

Disposition: a shared-catalog consistency fold (OLMo-2 now resolves its qk-norm-rope preamble through the one FusedChain recipe family instead of a bespoke inline sequence); no isolated tok/s A/B (identical numerics, composite realization). The binding proof is the CPU RED-first byte-exact unit + (owed) the OLMo-2 SACRED gate holding on the DGX.
